A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GM-MoE study. All 14 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original GM-MoE benchmark evaluations, qualitative results, and ablations, including SID results, LPIPS comparisons, and expert analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendix A, including the benchmark comparisons and ablation results in Tables 1-6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same U-Net-like architecture, three expert networks, dynamic gating, shallow feature extraction block, and PSNR loss. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LOL-v1, LOLv2-Real, LOLv2-Synthetic, LSRW-Huawei, and LSRW-Nikon, retain the SID evaluation in Appendix A.3, and show the same object-detection example in Figure 7.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 and the qualitative comparisons. LLFormer was already evaluated in v4's Table 1; replacing its unresolved citation with [67] does not add a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same data splits, preprocessing, augmentation, batch size of 4, two million training iterations, and PSNR/SSIM evaluation. Appendix LPIPS comparisons and ablation protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, fixed-weight and alternative expert-combination experiments in Table 6, expert heatmaps in Figure 12, and qualitative case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the reported runner-up PSNR margins from 1.5 to 0.90 dB on LOL-v1 and from 1.24 to 0.76 dB on LOLv2-Real. These match the unchanged Table 1 values: GM-MoE versus LLFormer is 26.66 versus 25.76, and GM-MoE versus DPEC is 23.65 versus 22.89. The 0.11 dB synthetic-data margin and all tabulated results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(8), covering expert weighting, interpolation, feature fusion, and the loss definition, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, adaptive-expert, generalization, and benchmark-superiority claims. The corrected numerical margins in Section 4.2 do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of enhancement quality, expert complementarity, and generalization remain unchanged. Appendix A.9 retains the same discussion of computational complexity, downstream applications, and alternative losses.

D1.justification: The PyTorch implementation, NVIDIA 4090 hardware, hyperparameters, processing instructions, and code-access information are unchanged. Appendix A.7 retains the same 27.2 GFLOPs disclosure.

R1.justification: The cited literature and research positioning are unchanged. Table 1's repaired LLFormer citation points to reference [67], already present and cited in v4's Table 5; bibliography changes only update citation-location references.

P1.justification: Figure 1's caption corrects GE-MoE to GM-MoE and fixes punctuation placement. Table 1 resolves the LLFormer citation, while the narrative wording and section organization otherwise remain unchanged apart from the numerical correction.

P2.justification: Table 2 newly highlights Restormer's four runner-up PSNR/SSIM scores in blue without changing their values. Figure 1's caption cleanup accompanies small layout reflow across pages 1-5. Figures, table structures, and appendix displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects overstated PSNR advantages to the Table 1-supported margins of 0.90 and 0.76 dB, improving numerical accuracy. The resolved LLFormer citation, corrected model name, and runner-up highlighting also improve presentation. These are useful but limited corrections; the underlying method, experiments, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
